sentences.text: Its skull was roughly triangular and covered in small pits when viewed from above.
The jaws held many small, pointed teeth that were laterally compressed and serrated.
Each maxilla contained 17 teeth, a high count among sebecians after Stolokrosuchus.
Researchers including Diogenes A. Campos and Alexander W.A. Kellner named the animal in 2011.
The genus name Pepesuchus honors Professor José Martin Suárez, nicknamed "Pepe", and combines it with the Greek word for crocodile.
The species name deiseae honors the paleontologist Deise Dias Rêgo Henriques.
It is classified with the peirosaurids Peirosaurus, Lomasuchus, and Uberabasuchus based on shared characteristics.
Pepesuchus belongs to the parent group Pepesuchinae.
The animal is classified within the family Peirosauridae.
Pepesuchus lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous in what is now the state of São Paulo, Brazil.
Other estimates suggest it lived from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
